=== scripts/assess/assess_cell.py
scripts/assess/assess_cell.py — the determination engine (rule_version: `RULE_VERSION` below).

THE STATE IS COMPUTED. Owner ruling 2026-09-09 (references/project-standards.md):
*"you have to compute it. I can't handle this load manually."* That supersedes
DR-2026-08-19 §12.5's "permanently manual" clause as it applies to `specifications`,
on contact (CLAUDE.md rule 0). Two sessions had read §12.5 as retiring this engine;
that reading is closed. What §12.5 still governs is untouched: the reasoning doc, the
Opus floor on best_practice_synthesis, the B-before-E gate — and this engine still
REFUSES data/guidebook.db outright and emits SQL for replay through
=== scripts/research/retrieval_log.py
scripts/research/retrieval_log.py — persist what was actually retrieved.

WHY
---
On 2026-08-19 the first research batch after the restart wrote FABRICATED author
lists onto all five of its admissions, and stamped them
`verification_status='VERIFIED'`, `verified_by_tool='crossref'`,
`verification_method='tool'`, `metadata_quality='COMPLETE'`.

=== scripts/research/mining_screen.py
Derive a citation-mining yield from a persisted payload and a NAMED screen.

CLAUDE.md rule 7a: a number is written as the command that computes it. A mining yield
is a number, and until 2026-09-18 it was produced by a regex typed into a shell and
recorded nowhere -- so two batches compared counts from two different instruments, a
pre-registered floor was scored against a screen it was not calibrated on, and a
retraction was published without re-deriving the anchor that founded the claim.

This is that command. It reads the screen from `governance/mining-screens.yaml` (the
=== scripts/research/full_text.py
Derive the WHOLE text of a source's held PDF or web page, registered under its ref_id.

WHY THIS EXISTS (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.3 step 1; tooling T1, owner approval D8,
2026-10-09). The scan contract reads every admitted source against the whole parameter
list, and a reading can only be as complete as the text it reads. Batch 23 extracted text
by hand from PDFs it held whole -- REF-01027's derived text covers 4 of its 79 pages -- and
nothing could say how much of a document a reading had actually seen. A reading recorded
as `full` over four pages would make the catalogue imply "no code sets a requirement"
where nobody read the code (the GAP-061 shape). This derives ALL pages, in the page-marker
=== scripts/research/page_image.py
Render a page of a persisted PDF to an image, so a session can LOOK at the scan.

WHY THIS EXISTS, AND IT IS A DEFECT REPORT ON BATCH 19 RATHER THAN A FEATURE NOTE.

Batch 19 mined REF-01005's bibliography out of a scanned 1979 microfiche. The PDF's OCR
text layer is badly damaged, so the batch:

  * recorded "no OCR engine is available in this environment (no tesseract, no
    pdftotext), so this text layer is the best that exists here";
=== scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py
scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py — capture a research batch out of a scratch DB.

DR-2026-08-19 §12.0 (F3). The research write path is a session-scoped scratch
copy of the database: `db.py` writes to it under GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, so every
write-time refusal stays live (R9 duplicate-DOI lookups, H05/H07, CHECK
constraints, real exec_id allocation) instead of being reimplemented against a
renderer. This tool then extracts the delta as SQL, which feeds the ordinary
`emit_data_migration.py --input` and its ENUM/RANGE guards.

=== scripts/generate/context_map.py
scripts/generate/context_map.py — emit governance/context-map.yaml.

WHAT THIS IS. A machine-readable orientation index: where everything is, what it
is, who writes it, who reads it, and whether it is canonical or derived. It exists
so a fresh session can answer "what is this and can I trust it?" from one query
instead of by grepping a tree that hides six directories from ripgrep.

WHY IT IS GENERATED AND NOT WRITTEN. This repository's signature defect is a
document that is readable and wrong: a comment asserting a protection that was
=== scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py
scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py -- build the owner's browser page.

WHAT THIS IS. One HTML file that opens the guidebook database inside the viewer (sql.js, WebAssembly), so the
owner can read every table, follow every pointer and see what is waiting on them, from a phone. The request and
the owner's answer on the code it adds: references/project-standards.md, "Owner statement 2026-10-28".

WHAT IT INJECTS. The page derives tables, columns, keys, pointers and views from the embedded database. It cannot
derive four things, each read from its single home: the stage of a table (governance/stage-map.yaml), the
vocabularies and CHECK shapes (dbcore.check_values / check_expression), the determinations a source holds up
=== scripts/emit_data_migration.py
scripts/emit_data_migration.py — create a properly-named data-migration file.

Per GAP-290 resolution. The migration system (scripts/migrate_db.py) requires
data migrations to be named:

    scripts/migrations/data_{YYYYMMDDHHMMSS}_{session-slug}.sql

This script generates one for you. Two concurrent sessions will produce files
with different timestamps and can both land cleanly on `main`.
=== scripts/migrate_db.py
scripts/migrate_db.py — Run pending migrations against guidebook.db.

Spec: architecture/sqlite-data-layer.md §7 (schema) + governance/concurrent-write-architecture-proposal-2026-05-11.md (data).

Handles BOTH migration types:

1. Schema migrations: `scripts/migrations/NNN_*.sql` (numeric prefix).
   Tracked via PRAGMA user_version. Forward-only.

import re,sqlite3,yaml,datetime,sys
R='/home/user/guidebook/'
con=sqlite3.connect('file:'+R+'data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True)
sm=yaml.safe_load(open(R+'governance/stage-map.yaml'))['tables']
ct=yaml.safe_load(open(R+'governance/pipeline-contract.yaml'))
uv=con.execute('pragma user_version').fetchone()[0]
cnt={t:con.execute(f'select count(*) from "{t}"').fetchone()[0] for t in sm}
live={r[0] for r in con.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table'")}
# UNWRITABLE
empty={t for t in live if con.execute(f'select count(*) from "{t}"').fetchone()[0]==0}
unw=[]
for t in sorted(live):
    dead={f[3] for f in con.execute(f'PRAGMA foreign_key_list("{t}")') if f[2] in empty}
    for c in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")'):
        if c[1] in dead and c[3]: unw.append(f'{t}.{c[1]}')
# writers: db.py subcommand -> tables
src=open(R+'scripts/db.py').read()
fn={m.group(1):m.start() for m in re.finditer(r'^def (\w+)\(',src,re.M)}
order=sorted(fn.items(),key=lambda x:x[1])
def fbody(n):
    s=fn[n]; nx=[p for _,p in order if p>s]; return src[s:(nx[0] if nx else len(src))]
W=r'(?:INSERT(?:\s+OR\s+\w+)?\s+INTO|UPDATE|DELETE\s+FROM)\s+"?([a-z_]+)"?'
def deep(n,seen):
    if n in seen or n not in fn: return set()
    seen.add(n); b=fbody(n)
    t={m for m in re.findall(W,b,re.I) if m in sm}
    for c in re.findall(r'\b([a-z_]\w+)\(',b):
        if c in fn and c!=n: t|=deep(c,seen)
    return t
i=src.index('if args.command == "migrate"')
parts=re.split(r'\n    (?:el)?if args\.command == "([\w-]+)":',"\n    if args.command == \"migrate\":"+src[i+len('if args.command == "migrate":'):])
cmd={}
for k in range(1,len(parts),2):
    name,text=parts[k],parts[k+1]
    t={m for m in re.findall(W,text,re.I) if m in sm}
    for c in re.findall(r'\b([a-z_]\w+)\(',text):
        if c in fn: t|=deep(c,set())
    cmd[name]=t
cmd['add-locator']={'source_locators'}; cmd['unmined-gaps']=set()   # branch text bleeds into the file tail; checked by hand
# writers by table (db.py)
wr={}
for c,ts in cmd.items():
    for t in ts: wr.setdefault(t,[]).append(c)
def stage_tables(s): return sorted(t for t,v in sm.items() if v==s)
def tbl(s):
    rows=['| Table | Rows | Written by (`db.py`) |','|---|---:|---|']
    for t in stage_tables(s):
        w=', '.join(f'`{x}`' for x in sorted(wr.get(t,[]))) or '— no `db.py` verb (migration-seeded or other script)'
        rows.append(f'| `{t}` | {cnt[t]} | {w} |')
    return '\n'.join(rows)
def checks(s):
    st=[x for x in ct['stages'] if x['id']==s]
    if not st: return '_None in the contract._'
    rows=['| Criterion | Kind | Check |','|---|---|---|']
    for k in st[0].get('criteria',[]):
        rows.append(f"| `{k['id']}` | {k['kind']} | {('`'+k['check']+'`') if k.get('check') else '**none — unenforced**'} |")
    return '\n'.join(rows)
def cmds(s,extra=()):
    c=sorted(x for x,ts in cmd.items() if ts and all(sm[t]==s for t in ts))
    return ', '.join(f'`{x}`' for x in c)
# views spanning
views=[]
for n,sql in con.execute("select name,sql from sqlite_master where type='view' order by name"):
    refs=set(re.findall(r'(?:FROM|JOIN)\s+"?([a-z_]+)"?',sql,re.I))
    st=sorted({sm[r] for r in refs if r in sm})
    views.append((n,st))
def vw(s): return ', '.join(f'`{n}`' for n,st in views if st==[s]) or '—'
cross='\n'.join(f"| `{n}` | {' + '.join(st)} |" for n,st in views if len(st)>1)
today=datetime.date.today().isoformat()

def fbody(n):
    s=fn[n]; nx=[p for _,p in order if p>s]; return src[s:(nx[0] if nx else len(src))]
W=r'(?:INSERT(?:\s+OR\s+\w+)?\s+INTO|UPDATE|DELETE\s+FROM)\s+"?([a-z_]+)"?'

    for c in re.findall(r'\b([a-z_]\w+)\(',b):

    return t

for k in range(1,len(parts),2):

    t={m for m in re.findall(W,text,re.I) if m in sm}
    for c in re.findall(r'\b([a-z_]\w+)\(',text):

The reference is written to `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/a45ca7d3-e506-5935-9bfc-36628e89637d/scratchpad/pipeline-stages.md`, about 350 lines. It has one section per stage (base, research, evidence, judgment, synthesis, specification, render) plus `infrastructure`, which the stage map says is not a stage. Each section covers what the stage holds, its actions, scripts, skills, tables, views, and gate checks. A closing section lists the cross-stage views.

I generated it with `gen_stages.py` in the same scratchpad folder (full path: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/a45ca7d3-e506-5935-9bfc-36628e89637d/scratchpad/gen_stages.py`). The tables, row counts, `db.py` verbs and checks are derived from the live database and repository. Re-run the script rather than trusting the counts after the next migration (rule 7a).

**Limits** (also listed at the end of the file)
- **Table-to-stage is judged, not derived.** The stage map says no derivable edge exists. It also records that the placement of `gaps` is disputed, and I followed the map.
- **The "Written by" column lists `db.py` verbs only.** `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` also writes `specifications`, both specification link tables, the convergence tables and `gaps`. That is why `specifications` shows only `retire-specification`. `emit_batch_sql.py` writes `evidence_sources` and `source_slug_links`, which also don't appear in the column.
- **I read the verb-to-table mapping out of `db.py` with a regex.** I fixed `add-locator` and `unmined-gaps` by hand because their branch text bleeds into the end of the file. A verb that builds its SQL dynamically would be missed.
- **The skill assignments are mine.** They come from each skill's description and are recorded nowhere in the repository. CLAUDE.md §1 warns that some skills still presuppose the deleted item layer.

You attack the claim. You have no write access and you do not propose repairs —
proposing the fix is how a critic talks itself into accepting the thing.

**What you are looking for, in this order:**

1. **A gate that passed having examined nothing.** This repository's
   most-produced defect, four separate times. For every check cited as evidence,
   ask what its SUBJECT was. `EXAMINED: 0` under a PASS is not a pass. A session
   id in the wrong form (`.md` where the DB holds a bare stem) scopes a gate to
   zero rows and reports green.
2. **A number that could be wrong tomorrow with nothing going red.** Literals,
   thresholds, `min_items`, lists, globs, and sentences of prose restating a
   checked value. Prose callers are swept by no gate at all. Recompute every
   figure you are asked to accept.
3. **A claim the artifact does not support.** Read the artifact, not the summary
   of it. A 0-row object is unproven, not clean.

---COMMIT

    python3 scripts/ci_helpers/check_commit_msg.py --selftest

Exit codes: 0 = pass or exempt, 1 = fail, 2 = cannot run.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from commit_gate import is_bot, is_merge  # noqa: E402

PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]+:\s+.+\s+\[\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\s+\d{2}:\d{2}\]$")


def git(*args):
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout.strip(), proc.stderr.strip()


def evaluate(message, author, parent_count):
    """Pure decision function — no git, so the selftest can drive it directly.
    Returns (exit_code, explanation)."""
    if is_bot(author):
        return 0, f"E3: bot commit ({author}) — format exempt."
    if is_merge(parent_count):
        return 0, "E4: merge commit — format exempt."
    if PATTERN.match(message or ""):
        return 0, "PASS: commit message format valid."
    return 1, ("FAIL: commit message does not match required format\n"
               f"  Got:      {message!r}\n"
               "  Expected: {skill-name}: {action} [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]\n"
               "  Example:  workplan-orchestrator: update gap register [2026-04-18 14:30]")

---
name: run-pipeline
description: >
  Run the Accessible Built Environments pipeline end to end for a topic: research across languages and
  jurisdictions, evidence admission, judgment, synthesis, specification, render, then an adversarial audit
  of accuracy, logic and sequence. Variant `from-evidence` starts at evidence (sources already held, in
  hand or named by ref_id) and skips research. ALWAYS use when asked to "run the pipeline", "research
  <slug> end to end", "process these sources through to specifications", "evidence and beyond", or
  "from evidence onward". Not for single-stage work: use the stage's own skill or `db.py` verb.
---
**Invocation.** `/run-pipeline <slug-or-topic>` runs everything. `/run-pipeline from-evidence <ref_ids | file | DOI list>`
skips research. Everything below is the stage order; a stage is finished when its verification passes, not when its
rows are written. **Re-entry is normal** (new leads go back to research, a new concept back to base), but record
why. Every figure here is derived from the repo; do not paste counts.

**Open once, before the first Bash call:** `bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh`, `/session-open`, `/orient`. Work on a
scratch DB (CLAUDE.md §4 write path). Rules R1–R17 (SessionStart contract), CLAUDE.md §2 and
`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` govern; this file orders the work, it does not restate them. Verbs are listed by
`python3 scripts/db.py --help`; if one is missing, stop and file a GAP (rule 10).

## 1. base — read it before touching a source
The catalogue every source is read against: `base_parameters` + `terms`/`term_aliases`, the four lenses
(`base_taxonomy_identity`, `access_needs`, `base_icf`, `base_taxonomy_medical`), `slugs`, `lang_jur_map`.
- Work from ICF/access-need frame, **codes AND names**; never bare axis codes or population umbrellas.
- **Equivalence before minting.** Search terms and aliases first. A synonym is `add-alias`; a duplicate parameter is
  `merge-parameter`; a new concept is `observe-term` → `adjudicate-term` → `add-parameter` (or `decline-parameter` with
  the reason). Claude may *propose* parameters or lens rows; the proposal is a written adjudication with its source,
  not a silent insert. A parameter needs `set-parameter-direction` before stage 6 can use it.
- Check: `scripts/validate_parameters.py`, `scripts/validate_schema.py`.

## 2. research — by topic, across languages and jurisdictions *(skipped by `from-evidence`)*
- Coverage is **slug × language × jurisdiction** from `lang_jur_map`; native-language terms come from the keyword
  compendium, never from memory (R11). Co-1 / T2 / Co-2 pass first (R1).
- **Every query is logged before screening** with `log-search --prior-expectation …` (R8); empties are kept and
  classified query-shape / wrong index / genuine absence (R14). `coverage` and the `v_coverage_*` views show what is
  unsearched. Skills: `multilingual-research`, `functional-deficit-researcher`, `research-log-manager`.
- **Citation mining** of every confirmed T1–T2 anchor, backward and forward, to the depth R2 requires:
  `citation-miner`, yields via `scripts/research/mining_screen.py`; open gaps via `gap-driven-mining`.
- Candidates go through `add-candidate` / `resolve-candidate`; leads into `add-locator`, `add-code-lead`.
- Check: `search_log_completeness.py`, `citation_mining_completeness.py`.

## 3. evidence — admit, then read the whole source against the whole catalogue
- **Admit** only after R9 (DOI pre-check, cross-file the existing ref_id) and R10 (re-retrieve; a publisher block is
  not terminal; Wayback per CLAUDE.md §7). Persist every payload with `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py`; write
  bibliographic fields **from the payload**, then `--verify-authors`. `add-source`; `link-source-slug` to every slug
  the source bears on.
- **Record all bibliographic data:** every author (Co-1 co-authors are the warrant, never dropped), year, title,
  venue, DOI/PMID/ISBN/standard number, URL, tier, retrieval and verification status. Unverified is a value; say it.
- **The slug guides the search, not the reading.** Derive full text (`scripts/research/full_text.py`), read it against
  **every** parameter and lens, not only the slug that found it, and `record-scan --mode catalogue`. That row, with
  `observe-term` for each phrase the source uses (verbatim, unjudged) and `link-source-slug` for each topic it
  touches, is the source's list of everything relevant it contains. Unscanned parameters are debt:
  `scripts/audit/scan_debt.py`, `v_scan_ledger`.
- File economics and case studies in their tables (R12), never in prose.
- Check: `metadata_integrity_audit.py`, `provenance_artefact_audit.py`, `observation_verbatim_audit.py`.

## 4. judgment — assign populations, access needs, ICF codes; store figures so later stages can use them
*(Your "evidence stage adjudication" lives here: CLAUDE.md §6 records the owner's 2026-08-27 ruling that the
lens crossing is judgment's output. Moving it earlier needs a ruling and a `stage-map.yaml` change.)*
- `adjudicate-term` for every observed phrase (NOT-OURS and DEFERRED are answers). `add-extraction` per stated
  figure: parameter, the lens columns (identity, access need, ICF code+name, medical), typed value and unit, verbatim
  claim, locator, `figure_role`, `claim_type`. No locator → `[UNVERIFIED-QUANT]` (R3).
- `relate-extraction` for comparators; `derive-extraction` for computed base+delta figures; `raise-follow-up` for
  doubtful rows. `add-population-match` grades population-of-study vs population-served (R13; children, general
  population and no-participants are PROXY); a dissenting grade is a second row.
- Capture failure, harm and inadequacy as first-class rows (R7).
- Output must be usable *without re-reading the source*: a render or a determination reads the typed row and its
  locator, nothing else.
- Check: `judgment_handoff_shape.py`, `extraction_relations_integrity.py`, `adjudication_integrity.py`.

## 5. synthesis — read rows against each other *(Opus-class only for `best_practice_synthesis`)*
- For each parameter cluster, ask which **other** parameters, populations or equipment change it. Example: swept-path
  figures for different wheelchairs set different turning spaces, corridor widths and door approaches. Make each such
  dependency a row: `add-connection` (mechanism stated), `derive-extraction` where one figure is computed from
  another, `add-conflict` where populations pull opposite ways (`cross-population-conflict-mapper`).
- **Independence:** sources sharing a root are one source (`v_value_independence`, `external_root_registry`).
  `connection-discovery`, `supersession-audit` (`add-supersession-check`), `add-gap` for what is missing.
- Reasoning documents under `references/connection-reasoning/` need an attestation (rule 2).

## 6. specification — best practice is the most accommodating, not the most common
- The state is **computed**: `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` (see `--help`) per cell, on the scratch DB. Do not
  hand-assign. Then review the output against these tests; a failure is a gate or a GAP, never a hand edit:
  1. **Most accommodating, gentlest, most dignified** value, read by the parameter's direction
     (`higher_is_better` / `lower_is_better`). `contested` means no single value: render the spread with each
     population's direction stated. Frequency of a value is never evidence for it; mode, median and count appear
     nowhere in the rationale.
  2. **Code is a floor.** T4–T6 alone yields a regulatory-stratum claim (`code_floor_only` when T6-only), never best
     practice. A code value stands as best practice only when T1 / Co-1 / T2 / Co-2 evidence directly backs it.
     Expect best practice from academic research, clinical guidelines and advocacy groups.
  3. Rationale states what the value does for the disabled people it serves, with the marker (●/◐/○) and tier mix.
  4. An engine defect is fixed in a tooling-only PR (rule 10), not worked around in the batch.
- `raise-determination-gate` caps a cell at provisional; `retire-specification` reopens one.
- Check: `validate_evidence_state.py`, `derivation_handshake_integrity.py`, `medical_lens_integrity.py`.

## 7. render — read from the database at render time; commit nothing generated
There is no committed renderer; write output to the scratchpad (publish only if asked). From specifications and
`v_determination_provenance`, `v_source_reach_all`, `v_best_practice`:
- web-readable prose per specification, value first, then rationale;
- **a comparison table of all evidence** for the parameter: every extraction, dissent included, with tier, lens,
  population-match grade, locator and verification status, plus sources scanned and **left out, and why**;
- **radical transparency:** direction, rule version, derivation, gates, code-floor flags, gaps and `[UNVERIFIED]`
  items stated on the page, not omitted;
- bibliography via `bibliography-compiler` from `evidence_sources` and `evidence_source_authors`; full author lists,
  DOI links; no citation for a source not in the table.
- Check: `matrix_consistency.py`.

## 8. adversarial audit — a separate critic, then repair
Run `/adversarial` (the `antagonist` agent; never self-review). Brief it with three questions and have it return
`[NULL: …]` where it finds nothing:
- **Accuracy:** do stored bibliographic fields match the payload bytes; does each figure match its locator; do
  cited sources exist? Lenses `L1-existence`, `L2-fidelity`, `S2-mismatch-note-vs-payload`.
- **Logic:** do converging sources share a root; is the tier right; does population-of-study fit population-served;
  was contrary evidence found; does any determination rest on frequency or on code alone? `L3`–`L6`.
- **Sequence:** every row's pointers resolve to rows from an earlier stage; no extraction on an unadmitted or
  unverified source; no determination before direction, extractions and convergence exist; no stage verified
  after the stage that consumed it. **No recorded lens covers sequence** (derive the set with
  `dbcore.check_values(conn, 'adversarial_findings', 'lens')`); record these as method, and file a GAP if it should
  become a lens.
Then `/batch-done`. Under `from-evidence`, `search_log_completeness` correctly reports NOTHING-IN-SCOPE.

## Finish
`scripts/preflight.sh` once, `run_checks.py --selftest` after any rename, commit scratchpad and transcripts
(rule 6), open the PR last and `unsubscribe_pr_activity` at once (rule 9). Research rows and tooling ship in
separate PRs (rule 10).

entries.description: List pull requests in a GitHub repository. If the user specifies an author, then DO NOT use this tool and use the search_pull_requests tool instead.

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each pull request. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

head.description: Filter by head user/org and branch

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

entries.name: mcp__github__pull_request_read
entries.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

name: spec-page-requirements
description: "Owner's stated requirements for specification pages (jurisdiction accordions, 3 value tiers, population/ICF/need filters, unit selector, plain-language labels) and how they were implemented in the E-03 pilot."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d9505991-620e-4974-95b2-b407384c5793
  modified: 2026-10-29T18:42:55.738Z
---

Owner requirements for the spec pages (stated 2026-10-29 while reviewing sample pages), implemented as a pilot on **E-03** (`site/specs/e-03.html`, generated by `scripts/generate/spec_page_v2.py` from `data/spec_pages/E-03.json` + the DB):

- **Jurisdiction comparison must be exhaustive**, as accordions: top line = jurisdiction + salient standard/clause/value/note; expansion = everything else. Every jurisdiction in the search roster is listed, including "no entry yet".
- **Values are never a bare range under "ALL".** Three tiers (matches `design_scale` in migration 024): *for everyone* (ALL = universal, not a population), *for a specific group / ICF code / access need*, *for one person*. Each value must say who it is for.
- **Filter by population, ICF code, access need** (driven by migration 026 tables `icf_codes`, `access_needs`, `population_icf_map`, `source_*_tags`).
- **Unit selector** per page: metric/imperial/as-stated length; slope as ratio/percent/degrees/as-stated. Values are stored as structured numbers (tokens `{{slope=..|..}}`, `{{len=mm|..}}`), never baked into text.
- **No jargon** for users: "Mode P/S/Universal Mode" replaced by plain tier labels.
- **"Why it matters" = bullets with line breaks**, each tagged by where its evidence lives (in library / outside library / regulatory).
- A page's title must be the item name (never the BPC slug); A-01's page was wrong because its header/value came from a different record (threshold-door-hardware) than its text.

**Why:** the owner wants pages usable by policy and design audiences who cannot decode internal codes, and every figure traceable to who it serves and how it was verified.

**How to apply:** new/regenerated spec pages should follow `spec_page_v2.py`; only the E-03 pilot exists. The 72 other `site/specs` pages carry an "under review" banner and still show the old, wrong layout. ICF/need vocabularies and all source tags are PROVISIONAL/UNREVIEWED (see [[project-end-goal]], [[contract-traceability-invariant]]); only US ADA text was verified from a primary source for E-03.

**Jurisdiction scope (owner, 2026-10-29):** "buckets 1 and 2" = the leading jurisdictions (e.g. Canada, USA, Australia, Japan, Norway, etc.) plus a second group (e.g. Italy, China, etc.). The exact lists are not recorded anywhere in the repo or DB; ask the owner to confirm before treating any list as definitive. Order of work: (1) extract everything possible from the current codes/standards of all jurisdictions; (2) then look for higher-tier evidence (T1-T3, any language, any jurisdiction) for a
**Where the jurisdiction definition lives (found 2026-10-29):** `workplan/workplan-jurisdiction-sweep.md` (priority groups P1 Core US UK AU CA DE NO SE ISO EU; P2 Extended European FR CH NL DK FI BE IE ES IT PT; P3 Asia-Pacific JP SG NZ KR CN; P4/P5 Global South) and `governance/jurisdiction-philosophy.md` (24 canonical jurisdictions + ISO/EU meta-codes, selection criteria). The owner's "bucket 1/2" examples (CA US AU JP NO, then IT CN) cut across the P-groups, so the exact cut is still unconfir
**Master comparison table (owner, 2026-10-29):** for ramp gradient (and by extension any item with a numeric value) the page also needs an easy comparison master table: one row per jurisdiction showing the value it has (preferred, absolute maximum and its condition, run/rise between landings, verification level), unit-selector aware, above the detailed accordions.
**No "Not set" rows (owner, 2026-10-29):** a population/group value card whose status is "no evidence / Not set" must not be shown on the page at all. Absence of a card is the signal; only render values that have content. (Applies to value cards; the staged data may keep the placeholder.)
**Citations (owner, 2026-10-29):** every "In the library" reference is shown as an APA in-text citation (author or body + year), clickable; the popup shows the full APA bibliographic citation and, under the entry, lists all pages where that source has been cited. Do not show raw REF-ids as the visible label.
**No "outside the library" evidence (owner, 2026-10-29):** evidence is binary: either we have it (recorded in the library) or we do not. The library is simply what has been recorded. Anything found and relied on must be ingested and cited like any other source; never label evidence as "outside the library" or "external" on a page.
**Countries shown (owner, 2026-10-29):** show only the major identified countries for now (the P1+P2+P3 set from workplan/workplan-jurisdiction-sweep.md: US UK AU CA DE NO SE ISO EU; FR CH NL DK FI BE IE ES IT PT; JP SG NZ KR CN). Do not list the rest of the 47-code roster (e.g. Brazil) on the page; keep their data staged.
**Design (owner review, 2026-10-29, supersedes any earlier note):** do NOT use the site's `assets/guidebook.css` look (cream/yellow palette, Roboto Slab, JetBrains Mono): owner dislikes it. Take only the *information organisation* from the book era (plain jurisdiction tables with a Guidebook row, terse value-first bullets, one evidence line). Style rules: neutral white/grey with one blue accent (never yellow/cream), ONE system sans typeface, five type sizes only (32/24/18/16/14), 3 weights, no u
**ACCESSIBILITY IS A HARD CONSTRAINT (owner, 2026-10-29):** all site work must comply with web accessibility standards and best practices: WCAG 2.2 AA minimum plus COGA (project standard in governance/armature_v3_review.md). Wins any conflict with aesthetics. Itemised, testable list in audits/spec-page-design-requirements-2026-10-29.md section 6a; never self-certify compliance, record what was actually tested.
**Design analysis (2026-10-29):** the consolidated reconciliation of all owner design feedback is audits/spec-page-design-requirements-2026-10-29.md. It supersedes the scattered design notes above; redesign waits for the owner's answers to its section 8.
**DEFINITION OF BEST PRACTICE (owner, 2026-10-29, stated repeatedly; supersedes any "Guidebook position/working position"):** the Guidebook takes no positions. Best practice = the best way to do something according to how it benefits the intended group; it is NOT the most common or most agreed value. It is the most accommodating/gentlest value found in any current standard (including preferred values) unless an academic article or professional body improves on it. Never present "most common" or 
**Doctrines to honour on every spec page (read 2026-10-29):** governance/mission-and-epistemics.md (CANONICAL: thinking tool, questions-led, not a prescription manual, within-population variability, best practice by evidence hierarchy not code consensus, Co-1 co-primary), references/project-standards.md Core Doctrine (advocacy project not an authority: no "shall be"; every specification carries evidence marker ● evidence-based or ○ inferred; person tier = OT assessment), governance/audience-
**Pills (owner, 2026-10-29, relaxes the earlier "too many pills"):** pills are allowed if used judiciously (filter options, applied filters, similar controls). Only decorative or status pills are the trope to avoid.
**Minimalism must not cost legibility (owner, 2026-10-30):** especially for accessibility of website navigation. Navigation at least body size (16px+), dark, current location visible at load, visible control state; no small grey glyph cues. See audits/spec-page-design-defects-2026-10-30.md and requirements R16.

**Owner clarifications, 2026-10-30 (answers to my open confusions):**
- Two lenses: an AUDIENCE lens (designer, disabled person, OT, policymaker; changes which sections open by default, as in the e-08 exemplar) and a DISABILITY lens (population, ICF code, access need; the filters built so far). Only the disability lens exists on the v3 page; the audience lens is still to build.
- Buckets 1+2 are P1+P2+P3 (confirmed).
- "Covered" means the listed source has been read, had information extracted, and been VERIFIED. The page's "read" count is therefore not "covered"; currently 0 verified.
- Pages must ideally render directly from the database, not hand-staged JSON.
- "Specification" in the book and the item pages are the same idea: the correct way to design something.
- Best practice: the gentlest/most accommodating value found in practice IS best practice; no academic study is required (they are often unavailable). Existence in practice is the evidence. (This differs from the mission doc's "T4-T6 walled off from best-practice anchoring"; the owner's statement needs a doctrine decision record.)
- "Provisional" = the source must be re-read and the information confirmed; it is a review stage, not weak evidence. Provisional is a stage, not a permanent state.
- Tier numbering: governance/tier-system.md (OPERATIVE 2026-05-25) is the most recent and governs; project-standards line 17 and older notes are stale.
- Owner hypothesis on E-03: the problem is the lack of a rest landing, not the slope itself. The book spec pairs 1:20 with a rest platform every 9 m (>=1500x1500 mm); codes differ widely on landing spacing.

name: contract-traceability-invariant
description: "Hard requirement for the Guidebook — every boundary/handoff/IO at every stage and layer must have a verifiable, traceable contract."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d8ad22dd-b407-4f8b-b198-5ff102840966
---

A load-bearing requirement for the Guidebook pipeline: **at every single stage and layer — from the moment a website is visited and something of value is located, through every handoff — there must be a proper handshake/contract.** EVERY handshake / contract / handoff / exchange / input-output MUST be **verifiable** (you can mechanically check the contract held) AND **traceable** (you can follow provenance backward and forward across the boundary).

Boundaries this covers in the current system (non-exhaustive): runtime website request → data lookup → render; migration → DB (`data_migrations` ledger, `content_sha`); DB → Pydantic/JSON schema validation; DB → generated parts/site/vetting-surface; research → evidence collection (citation mining, probes, source/URL verification runs); evidence → judgment (directness, scope, tier, FDR, convergence, evidence_cell_state); judgment → synthesis → collation → rendering; governance

**Why:** This is the transparency guarantee that makes the output policy-grade and academically defensible (see [[project-end-goal]]). An untraceable or unverifiable handoff is a break in the evidence chain even if both sides are individually correct — it is treated as a defect of the same class as data corruption.

**How to apply:** When auditing or building, enumerate boundaries and for EACH ask: (1) Is there an explicit contract (schema/interface/ledger entry)? (2) Is conformance verifiable by a check, not by trust? (3) Is the exchange traceable end-to-end (provenance preserved, attributable, reproducible)? Any boundary that crosses data without all three is a finding. "Verifiable + traceable at every boundary" is a first-class audit dimension, not a nice-to-have.

**Sharpening — obscured transitions do the most damage.** The highest-risk boundaries are the ones nobody declared as boundaries: implicit couplings, hand-synced duplicate representations (DB ⇄ JSON register kept in sync manually), steps "applied out-of-band" (the ledger-only `data_migrations` rows where SQL was not re-executed), manual handoffs with no record (PI bump that only goes live when the owner pastes into claude.ai), silent field drops in `convert_*` mappings, and identifiers reuse

name: current-state-only
description: "Owner direction - the guidebook is about best practice NOW; use the current edition of each source and do not research or record history, superseded editions or edition-to-edition changes."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: d9505991-620e-4974-95b2-b407384c5793
  modified: 2026-10-30T00:35:24.554Z
---

The project is interested in what best practice is **now**. Use only the current in-force edition of each standard or code. Do not investigate or record how a provision changed over time, and do not read superseded editions.

**Why:** owner said (2026-10-29) "we do not need to interrogate the history of anything but rather the current state of everything".

**How to apply:** for each jurisdiction, find the current edition and read that; discard other editions (e.g. Singapore Code 2025, not 2019; Ireland TGD M 2022, not 2010). Do not add "changed from X" commentary to pages or findings. Edition identity still matters only so the cited text is the current one. Pairs with [[code-baselines-accepted]] (accept T4-T6 values as given).

- "Specification" in the book and the item pages are the same idea: the correct way to design something.

name: contract-traceability-invariant
description: "Hard requirement for the Guidebook — every boundary/handoff/IO at every stage and layer must have a verifiable, traceable contract."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d8ad22dd-b407-4f8b-b198-5ff102840966
---

A load-bearing requirement for the Guidebook pipeline: **at every single stage and layer — from the moment a website is visited and something of value is located, through every handoff — there must be a proper handshake/contract.** EVERY handshake / contract / handoff / exchange / input-output MUST be **verifiable** (you can mechanically check the contract held) AND **traceable** (you can follow provenance backward and forward across the boundary).

Boundaries this covers in the current system (non-exhaustive): runtime website request → data lookup → render; migration → DB (`data_migrations` ledger, `content_sha`); DB → Pydantic/JSON schema validation; DB → generated parts/site/vetting-surface; research → evidence collection (citation mining, probes, source/URL verification runs); evidence → judgment (directness, scope, tier, FDR, convergence, evidence_cell_state); judgment → synthesis → collation → rendering; governance

**Why:** This is the transparency guarantee that makes the output policy-grade and academically defensible (see [[project-end-goal]]). An untraceable or unverifiable handoff is a break in the evidence chain even if both sides are individually correct — it is treated as a defect of the same class as data corruption.

**How to apply:** When auditing or building, enumerate boundaries and for EACH ask: (1) Is there an explicit contract (schema/interface/ledger entry)? (2) Is conformance verifiable by a check, not by trust? (3) Is the exchange traceable end-to-end (provenance preserved, attributable, reproducible)? Any boundary that crosses data without all three is a finding. "Verifiable + traceable at every boundary" is a first-class audit dimension, not a nice-to-have.

**Sharpening — obscured transitions do the most damage.** The highest-risk boundaries are the ones nobody declared as boundaries: implicit couplings, hand-synced duplicate representations (DB ⇄ JSON register kept in sync manually), steps "applied out-of-band" (the ledger-only `data_migrations` rows where SQL was not re-executed), manual handoffs with no record (PI bump that only goes live when the owner pastes into claude.ai), silent field drops in `convert_*` mappings, and identifiers reuse

description: "Owner direction - the guidebook is about best practice NOW; use the current edition of each source and do not research or record history, superseded editions or edition-to-edition changes."

The project is interested in what best practice is **now**. Use only the current in-force edition of each standard or code. Do not investigate or record how a provision changed over time, and do not read superseded editions.

**Why:** owner said (2026-10-29) "we do not need to interrogate the history of anything but rather the current state of everything".

**How to apply:** for each jurisdiction, find the current edition and read that; discard other editions (e.g. Singapore Code 2025, not 2019; Ireland TGD M 2022, not 2010). ## Owner rulings 2026-10-30 — best practice, the specification page and rendering (from the ramp-slope session)

Given in the owner's local session `d9505991-620e-4974-95b2-b407384c5793` (exported as `session-export-1793395272333`, titled "Research pipeline stress test: ramp slopes"), on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30, after the entries above, and recorded here on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-30 to implement those decisions in the repository, per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 and workplan WR-3. The statements were found in the session transcript and are quoted verbatim; the reconciliation against `main` is `workplan/2026-10-30-ramp-spec-pages/RENDER-DECISIONS-AND-PIPELINE.md`.

On best practice and the specification:

- "best practice = the best way to do something according to how it benefits the intended group"
- "best practice =/= most common or agreed upon. we have been through this a million times"
- "remember that our guidebook doesn't take positions. it just presents what appears to be the most accommodating/gentle best practice for anything... so unless an academic article or some professional body improves upon germany's standard, that's identified as the best practice"

- "specification in book and item pages now are the same idea in that it tells you the correct way to design something"
- "the critical methodology comes from synthesis/adjudication/specifications, not from evidence collection"

On states, scope and sources:

- "...covered means that the source that has been listed in the database has been read and had information extracted from it then verified"
- "provisional means that we have to go back and review the source again to confirm information accuracy" (the owner's answer 10 reads "stage. provisional means that we have to go back and review the source again to confirm information accuracy")
- "how on earth do we have evidence outside the library? we either have evidence or we do not have evidence. our library is just what we have recorded"

On rendering and the page:

- "i want it to be coming from database directly in ideal world"
- "There is an audience lens (the four audiences) and a disability lens (population, ICF, access needs)"

**What this does.** The readings are the assistant's and are marked; the owner's words above are the ruling.

1. **Best practice is the most accommodating value found, not the commonest.** The value a determination names as best practice is the gentlest or most accommodating one found in practice, in the direction recorded for the parameter (`base_parameters.accessibility_direction`; for ramp gradient, lower is better), unless a study or a professional body improves on it. It is not the modal or the agreed value, and the steepest value a code allows is not highlighted. No study is needed for a value to be named, and a T4 to T6 value is accepted as a baseline without tracing its history. [ASSUMPTION: this ruling selects which value is named; it does not change the band or the flag. Under the 2026-07-21 owner directive (Option A, `governance/tier-system.md` section 8, `governance/evidence-architecture.md` I3), a determination resting on T4 to T6 alone is already stated as weak-band (○) "best pra
2. **Provisional is a stage; covered means read, extracted and verified.** A reading is provisional until its source has been read again and the information confirmed. A source counts as covered only when that has happened, so a page says "read, none yet verified" while no reading is verified, and lists the jurisdictions whose sources are not yet read as not yet read. [ASSUMPTION: this matches `specifications.state` (`pending`, `provisional`, `stated`) and `has_unverified_sources`; no new field is needed.]
3. **An item page is the specification.** The book's specification and the item pages are the same thing, and it is rendered from the database. [ASSUMPTION: "database directly" is read together with owner ruling OW-1 of 2026-10-29 (third), under which the render table holds the specification rows as prose with bibliographic information drawn from the preceding tables, and with the 2026-08-27 ruling that no committed file is a render. A static generator emitting committed HTML is therefore not restored; the mechanism the ramp session built is not carried, and its requirements are.]
4. **Two lenses.** A page offers an audience lens (designer, disabled person, occupational therapist, policy maker; `governance/audience-priority.md`) and a disability lens (population, ICF code, access need). Only the disability lens was built before. Lens filtering shows its more specific options only after a lens is chosen, and the controls come before the information.
5. **Page content and form.** A master comparison table gives one row per in-scope jurisdiction, alphabetical, with the standard and its edition under the row and the detail one click from the value. Rows with no value are not shown. Evidence is listed alphabetically by first author's last name and regrouped by the chosen lens. One sans typeface, few sizes, and no decoration are the visual direction; the working requirements, with acceptance tests, are `workplan/2026-10-30-ramp-spec-pages/reports/spec-page-design-requirements-2026-10-29.md`, and the owner took the defaults for its open questions Q1 to Q7 ("Use my defaults"). [ASSUMPTION: that file is a working baseline for the renderer, not a ratified specification.]
6. **Accessibility is a precondition.** WCAG 2.2 level AA wins over aesthetics, and navigation legibility is not traded for minimalism. Compliance is never self-certified: a page is described as having passed the tests that were run, on the date and build recorded, and no third-party scan or screen-reader pass has yet been run on any page.
7. **Scope of a page.** The jurisdictions shown are the major identified countries, P1+P2+P3 of the jurisdiction ranking, current editions only. [ASSUMPTION: "P1+P2+P3" is the ranking recorded in `workplan/2026-10-30-ramp-spec-pages/HANDOFF.md` section 3.]
8. **Rest landing is the second headline parameter for ramp gradient.** The owner's hypothesis is that the rest landing, not the slope, is the problem, and the owner agreed to add landing spacing as a second headline parameter. **Verdict: Partly.** The skill orders the seven stages correctly and names real verbs for most of them, but as written its `from-evidence` variant cannot pass `/batch-done`, its specification and render sections contradict owner rulings of 2026-10-29/30 that it never records as superseded, its "all bibliographic data" and "list of everything relevant" promises have no writer behind them, and its adversarial brief cannot produce a closable pass.

## Steelman

The strongest version of this skill is a 124-line *ordering* document that deliberately refuses to restate rules (line 18: "this file orders the work, it does not restate them"), delegating law to CLAUDE.md, the R1–R17 hook contract and `pipeline-contract.yaml`, and delegating mechanism to `db.py --help`. That is defensible on rule 7a grounds: every restated rule is a prose caller that drifts. Placing lens-crossing at judgment rather than evidence (lines 58–59) is defensible because it honours a recorded ruling over the owner's newer phrasing and tells the owner exactly what a change would cost. Making `from-evidence` a variant rather than a separate skill is defensible because evidence onward is identical either way. Computing the specification state and forbidding hand edits (line 81) is the 2026-09-09 ruling verbatim. Routing the audit to `/adversarial` with three named questions is defensible because it reuses RC4 rather than inventing a parallel review. I attack that version.

## 1. Logic

- **`/home/user/guidebook/skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md:115`** — "no determination before direction, extractions and convergence exist." `convergence_assessment` rows are written *by* the determination run (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py:2085` "INSERTs the determination -- plus any gap and convergence row"; INSERT at :2206). The precondition is unsatisfiable; a critic briefed with it flags every determination. `grep -n "convergence" scripts/assess/assess_cell.py | sed -n 1,5p`.
- **:71** — "Opus-class only for `best_practice_synthesis`." No table, view or column of that name exists (`sqlite_master` returns nothing; the string survives only in `decisions` rationale text seeded by migration 057). None of the synthesis verbs the section then names (`add-connection`, `add-conflict`, `add-supersession-check`, `add-gap`, `derive-extraction`) carries a model gate; `connections.opus_reviewed` exists and is never mentioned. The floor binds nothing.

The two clauses conflict with each other for the live corpus (every governing row on parameter 3 is T4–T6, `specifications.tier_basis`), and with the rulings in §5 below.
- **:108–118** — the brief lists lenses L1, L2, S2 and "L3–L6". `db.py close-adversarial-pass` "refuses until every lens is covered" and the CHECK holds eleven (`dbcore.check_values(conn,'adversarial_findings','lens')` — count it). ## 2. Sequencing

---
name: run-pipeline
description: >
  Run the Accessible Built Environments pipeline end to end for a topic: research across languages and
  jurisdictions, evidence admission, judgment, synthesis, specification, render, then an adversarial audit
  of accuracy, logic and sequence. Variant `from-evidence` starts at evidence (sources already held, in
  hand or named by ref_id) and skips discovery searching only. ALWAYS use when asked to "run the pipeline",
  "research <slug> end to end", "process these sources through to specifications", "evidence and beyond", or
  "from evidence onward". Not for single-stage work: use the stage's own skill or `db.py` verb.
---
**Invocation.** `/run-pipeline <slug-or-topic>` runs everything. `/run-pipeline from-evidence <ref_ids | file | DOI list>`
starts at stage 3. A stage is finished when its verification passes, not when its rows are written. Re-entry is
normal (a new lead goes back to research, a new concept to base); record why in the session record
(`session-consolidator`). Derive every figure; paste no counts.

**Open once:** `/session-open` first (it sets `CURRENT` before the first Bash call), then
`bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh`, then `/orient`. Work on a scratch DB (CLAUDE.md §4). This file orders the work;
R1–R17 (SessionStart contract), CLAUDE.md §2 and `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` are the law. If a verb or field you
need does not exist (`python3 scripts/db.py --help`), stop and file a GAP with `add-gap` (rule 10); never hand SQL.
If two rulings conflict, stop, name both and ask; the later live owner statement wins (rule 0), recorded in the ledger.

**Posture (DR-2026-07-21; owner 2026-10-30: "simply PRESENTING information without claiming correctness").** The
guidebook is a thinking tool, not an authority. Describe and attribute; show derivation, strength and disagreement;
never call a value correct, safe or adequate.

**Scope (OR-8, OR-12a, ledger 2026-10-30).** Exhaustion is per parameter, per bucket member (a jurisdiction **with its
associated language**). In scope: P1+P2+P3 of `workplan/workplan-jurisdiction-sweep.md`; Arabic, Bengali, Hindi and
Swahili are scoped out for now. **Current editions only.** T4–T6 values are accepted as baselines; do not trace their history.

## 1. base — read before touching a source
The catalogue every source is read against: `base_parameters` + `terms`/`term_aliases`, the lenses
(`base_taxonomy_identity`, `access_needs`, `base_icf`, `base_taxonomy_medical`), `slugs`, `lang_jur_map`. Codes AND names;
no bare axis codes or population umbrellas.
- **Equivalence before minting.** Search terms and aliases first. Synonym → `add-alias`; duplicate parameter →
  `merge-parameter`; otherwise a new concept.
- **A new concept arises while a source is in hand** (`observe-term` needs `--ref-id` and a quote from a persisted file),
  so base is re-entered from stages 3–4. Claude may *propose* a parameter or lens row; the owner names it. **Claude never
  generates a phrase, name or alias** (OR-17): it is the source's own wording, present in its jurisdiction and language.
  Put the proposal (source, quote, candidate equivalents) to the owner; `adjudicate-term`, `add-term`, `add-parameter` or
  `decline-parameter` follow their answer.
- `set-parameter-direction` records which way is better, **from an admitted source, never hand-set** (ledger 2026-10-30).
  Without it stage 6 cannot select a value.
- Checks: `validate_parameters.py`, `schema_reference_audit.py`, `identifier_floor_audit.py`.

## 2. research — by topic, across languages and jurisdictions *(skipped by `from-evidence`)*
- Coverage is slug × bucket member, bounded by Scope above. In-language terms come from `term_aliases` and the source's
  own words (R11); never from memory or back-translation. Co-1 / T2 / Co-2 first (R1). Skills: `multilingual-research`,
  `functional-deficit-researcher`, `research-log-manager`.
- **Log every query before screening:** `log-search --prior-expectation … --result-artefact <payload>` (R8). Without
  `--result-artefact` the query→payload link is missing. Keep empties. R14's class (query-shape / wrong index / genuine
  absence) has no column: put it in `findings_note`. `coverage` and the `v_coverage_*` views show what is unsearched.
- **Citation mining** of every confirmed T1–T3 anchor, backward and forward, to the depth R2 requires: `citation-miner`,
  yields via `scripts/research/mining_screen.py`; open gaps via `gap-driven-mining`.
- Candidates: `add-candidate`, `resolve-candidate`; leads: `add-locator`, `add-code-lead`.
- Checks: `search_log_completeness.py`, `citation_mining_completeness.py`.

## 3. evidence — admit, then read the whole source against the whole catalogue
- **Admit** after R9 (DOI pre-check) and R10 (re-retrieve; a block is not terminal, Wayback per CLAUDE.md §7). Persist

## 3. evidence — admit, then read the whole source against the whole catalogue

  book title, pages, DOI/PMID, URL, tier, evidence type, Co-1 provenance and verification; `correct-source` sets

## 5. synthesis — read rows against each other

  figure is computed from another, `add-conflict` where populations pull opposite ways.

## 6. specification — the most accommodating value found, not the most common
- The state is **computed**: `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` per cell on the scratch DB (it writes the convergence row
  and the determination together). Do not hand-assign. Review its output against these tests; a failure is a gate or a
  GAP, never a hand edit. A re-run for the same cell is refused: `retire-specification` first.
  1. Name the **most accommodating** value found in practice, read by the parameter's direction. `contested` means no
     single value: show the spread with each population's direction. Frequency is never evidence; the steepest value a
     code allows is never highlighted.
  2. **Code is the weakest tier, not disqualified** (Option A, tier-system §8; ledger 2026-10-30, ratified). A
     determination resting on T4–T6 alone may be named, at the weak band **○**, with the code-derived flag and the
     convergence-not-evidence caveat, and is **never ●**. Evidence that improves on it (academic research, clinical
     guidelines, advocacy and lived-experience work) replaces it and earns the stronger band. If the engine labels a
     code-only cell otherwise (its G1 branch comment says "never best practice"), that is an engine defect: tooling PR.
  3. The recorded rationale is the derivation (which sources, what they state, the rule version), not an endorsement.
- `raise-determination-gate` caps a cell at provisional.
- Checks: `validate_evidence_state.py`, `derivation_handshake_integrity.py`, `medical_lens_integrity.py`.

`/adversarial` (the `antagonist` agent; never self-review). Derive the lens set
(`dbcore.check_values(conn, 'adversarial_findings', 'lens')`); **a pass closes only when every lens is covered**, so
assign each to a question and omit none:

- **Logic:** shared roots, tier, population fit, contrary evidence, frequency or code standing in for evidence,
  posture. L3–L7, L8 (was a zero-yield search well-formed), S1, S3.
- **Sequence:** every pointer resolves to an earlier stage's row; no extraction on an unadmitted or unverified source;
  no determination without direction and extractions; no stage verified after its consumer ran. **No lens covers
  sequence**: record it as method, and file a GAP if it should become a lens.

+- **No check examines rendered output** (`register-invariants` has `check: null`): walk contract invariants I1–I6 by hand.
+
+## 8. adversarial audit — a separate critic, then repair
+`/adversarial` (the `antagonist` agent; never self-review). Derive the lens set
+(`dbcore.check_values(conn, 'adversarial_findings', 'lens')`); **a pass closes only when every lens is covered**, so
+assign each to a question and omit none:
+- **Accuracy:** stored bibliographic fields against the payload bytes, figures against locators, existence. L1, L2, S2.
+- **Logic:** shared roots, tier, population fit, contrary evidence, frequency or code standing in for evidence,
+  posture. L3–L7, L8 (was a zero-yield search well-formed), S1, S3.
+- **Sequence:** every pointer resolves to an earlier stage's row; no extraction on an unadmitted or unverified source;
+  no determination without direction and extractions; no stage verified after its consumer ran. **No lens covers
+  sequence**: record it as method, and file a GAP if it should become a lens.
+Then `/batch-done`. **`from-evidence` still faces its blocking gates:** R17 (a logged search per admission), R1 (a
+Co-1/Co-2 search or source, or a reasoned `CO1-NOT-APPLICABLE` in a search's `findings_note`) and R2 (`citation_mining`
+rows for admitted T1–T3 anchors). Mine the anchors; R10 fetches leave WebFetch ledger lines that
+`search_log_completeness` reads.
+
+## Resume and exceptions
+Resume from live state, not memory: `/orient`; unadjudicated observations (`observed_terms` with no
+`term_adjudications` row); `scan_debt.py`; open follow-ups; parameters with extractions and no live specification.
+The scratch DB is disposable and the canonical sha256 does not move until the migration applies, so a mid-batch failure
+costs only the unemitted rows. A blocked source: Wayback, else admit UNVERIFIED. A zero-yield search is a completed
+unit of work. Finish: `scripts/preflight.sh` once, `run_checks.py --selftest` after any rename, commit scratchpad and
+transcripts (rule 6), open the PR last and `unsubscribe_pr_activity` at once (rule 9); research rows and tooling ship in

content.text:
`workplan-orchestrator` is retired and `/run-pipeline` replaces it, in PR #214. I've unsubscribed from the PR, per rule 9. `scripts/preflight.sh` and `run_checks.py --selftest` both passed. Nothing was run through the skill itself, so it is untested in use.

The skill covers the seven stages in your order, then an adversarial audit of accuracy, logic and sequence. `/run-pipeline from-evidence` starts at evidence and skips discovery searching only. It still has to pass the blocking `/batch-done` gates: a logged search per admission, a Co-1/Co-2 search or source (or a recorded waiver), and citation mining for admitted T1–T3 sources. The new skill is 174 lines against the 327 it replaces. Preflight reported 9 advisory failures, which I didn't investigate.

**Your two instructions**
- **Render step:** it now points to the merged PRs on specification-page display: #205, #207, #208 and #210, plus #204 for the owner browser. It carries their rules: render from the database, no committed file, the renderer never composes a value, and "describe and attribute" voice. It also requires a master table with no valueless rows, WCAG 2.2 AA never self-certified, and APA citations with a cited-on list.
- **Code-only specifications:** step 6 now says what you said. A specification resting only on code can be named best practice at the weak band (○), with the code-derived flag, and is never ●. Better evidence replaces it. This matches the ratified 2026-10-30 ledger entry.

**Critic findings**
The Fable critic returned 20 findings, and I checked the main ones against the code before repairing. The worst: `from-evidence` could not have passed `/batch-done` as first written, and my original code-only clause contradicted the owner's ratified ruling. I also fixed or reworded bibliographic fields with no writer, coverage that ignored the OR-8/OR-12a scope rulings, a nonexistent keyword compendium, an unsatisfiable convergence precondition, and an adversarial brief that omitted four of the eleven lenses.

**Not fixed, left for you or a tooling PR**
- **Engine:** the `assess_cell.py` G1 comment says a code-only cell is "never best practice", and `v_best_practice` still filters out code-only rows. OR-7 says to drop that filter.
- **Missing writers:** journal name, ISBN, ISSN, standard number and edition cannot be entered through the CLI. The skill says to file a GAP and show "not recorded" on the page.
- **Item-layer skills:** `connection-discovery` and `cross-population-conflict-mapper` still presuppose the deleted item layer. The new skill uses their search method only.
- **Risk escalation:** the old skill's rule (two or more escalation signals append a REVIEW gap) has no live home. Whether to keep it is your call.
- **Doctrine still naming the old skill:** `governance/project-instructions-v10_14.md` and `governance/population-taxonomy.md` still name it; I left them unedited because they're doctrine.

[CONFIDENCE: medium — the critic's claims were checked on the points that changed the text, not all twenty line by line.]

CREATE TABLE adversarial_findings (
  finding_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  pass_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES adversarial_passes(pass_id),
  lens            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (lens IN (
                    'L1-existence','L2-fidelity','L3-independence','L4-tier','L5-population',
                    'L6-contrary','L7-recognition','L8-query-shape',
                    'S1-harm-reached-row','S2-mismatch-note-vs-payload','S3-containment')),
  subject_table   TEXT,                -- loose pointer to the row attacked; never a copy of it,
                                       -- and never FK-enforced -- see header, "not Layer 1"
  subject_key     TEXT,
  claim_attacked  TEXT NOT NULL,
  method          TEXT NOT NULL,
  artefact        TEXT,                -- what the claim was attacked WITH (DR-2026-09-11 clause 2)
  verdict         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (verdict IN
                    ('SUSTAINED','SURVIVED','NOT-ATTACKED','WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER')),
  severity        TEXT CHECK (severity IS NULL OR severity IN ('CRITICAL','HIGH','MEDIUM','LOW')),
                                       -- required iff verdict='SUSTAINED' (RULE ACTION 2)
  disposition     TEXT CHECK (disposition IS NULL OR disposition IN
                    ('REPAIRED','REJECTED','PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED','OWNER-RULED')),
  disposition_ref TEXT,                -- a data migration path; a quote-anchored ledger pointer; or the reason
  disposed_by_session TEXT,            -- NULL until disposed; set once, never overwritten (writer-enforced)
  disposed_at     TEXT,
  created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  -- The SUSTAINED<->severity pairing is a schema CHECK, not only a Python refusal, on
  -- the same precedent as `reviewer_transcript <> author_transcript` above: an invariant
  -- worth enforcing in a writer is worth enforcing for every future writer and every
  -- data migration that ever touches this table, not just the one call path that exists
  -- today. (severity IS NOT NULL) is 0/1 in SQLite, so this compares cleanly with the
  -- 0/1 of (verdict = 'SUSTAINED').
  CHECK ((verdict = 'SUSTAINED') = (severity IS NOT NULL))
) STRICT

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskList
entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

-- 115_identity_names.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- the identity lens registry and its ICF map take the lens's own name (plan Phase 3
-- base; RULINGS R14 narrowed to M4, confirmed in R49(c); LED-127, LED-121). `populations` is the
-- identity lens (owner, 2026-08-28), and its key was the one lens key still called population_code
-- while every referencing column already said identity_code.

--   population_icf_links         -> identity_icf_map         (population_code -> identity_code)

-- NOT IN THIS FILE: evidence_population_match and its target_population / study_population columns.
-- LED-127 names them served_group / study_group and keeps them out of the lens vocabulary, which R14's
-- evidence_identity_match contradicts; the name is the owner's. Renaming the table needs an
-- AFTER_DATA marker, because data migrations dated after 095 INSERT into it.
--
-- NO AFTER_DATA MARKER for the two renames above. Two facts together make that safe, and the second
-- is the operative one: (1) no committed data migration dated after the 095 cutoff names the renamed
-- objects (must print nothing; the literal is 095's cutoff, not today's):
--   grep -lwE 'populations|population_icf_links|population_code' scripts/migrations/data_*.sql | xargs -n1 basename | cut -d_ -f2 | awk '$1>"20260920060857"'
-- and (2) migrations 113 and 114 carry AFTER_DATA markers at the latest data_ timestamp, so
-- migrate_db.build_plan replays 115 after every committed data migration whatever it names. If (2)
-- ever changes, (1) is the check that must still hold.
--
-- SQLite rewrites every REFERENCES clause, the UNIQUE autoindex and the sqlite_sequence row itself;
-- idx_picf_icf keeps its name (there is no RENAME INDEX) and its column list is rewritten. No view and
-- no trigger names either table.

ALTER TABLE populations RENAME TO base_taxonomy_identity;
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_identity RENAME COLUMN population_code TO identity_code;
ALTER TABLE population_icf_links RENAME TO identity_icf_map;
ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map RENAME COLUMN population_code TO identity_code;

CREATE TABLE extraction_relations (
  relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

  -- THE FIGURE THIS EDGE QUALIFIES. NOT NULL and a real FK -- an edge naming no source
  -- row describes nothing. No UNIQUE index touches this column alone: one extraction may
  -- carry several comparator edges (a ramp slope is both condition_on a run-length limit
  -- AND audited_against a code's stated maximum), and collapsing that to one row per
  -- extraction would force a choice this table exists to avoid forcing.
  from_extraction_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),

  -- WHAT KIND OF COMPARISON THIS EDGE IS. Eight values; the CHECK is the vocabulary
  -- (CLAUDE.md section 4) and this is only its meaning, one line each.
  --   tested_at        -- the source physically measured its subjects at/against this
  --                      referent -- REF-00973's four ramp slopes were each tested_at a
  --                      named gradient.
  --   audited_against  -- the source measured whether subjects could perform WITHIN a
  --                      referent's own stated limit, rather than measuring an
  --                      independent value -- REF-00971's "existing standards".
  --   confirms         -- an independent measurement agrees with the referent's value.
  --   insufficient     -- the source asserts the referent's value is NOT ENOUGH for the
  --                      population or task in question -- REF-00784's 10-100% figure.
  --   exceeds          -- the source asserts the referent's value is more than needed.
  --   delta_over       -- the source states an increment relative to a baseline rather
  --                      than an absolute figure -- REF-00976's "more than thirty
  --                      centimetres of enlargement over the surveyed stock".
  --   condition_on     -- this figure only holds given a second figure this project also
  --                      holds as a row -- a slope given its run-length limit.
  --   derived_from     -- this figure is computed from the referent, never read off a
  --                      source -- always paired with input_role below and always a row
  --                      referent, never a label; see the CHECK immediately following.
  relation            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (relation IN (
                        'tested_at', 'audited_against', 'confirms', 'insufficient',
                        'exceeds', 'delta_over', 'condition_on', 'derived_from')),

  -- THE REFERENT, HALF A: a row this project already holds. Nullable -- see to_label.
  -- Self-joins

def schema_objects(conn):
    """Views, triggers and indexes, by name -> DDL.

    Rows are not the whole database. `v_best_practice` (migration 027/029) carries
    the convergence-laundering exclusion in its WHERE clause, so editing that view
    in the committed DB changes what the project treats as a best-practice claim
    while leaving every row identical. A row-only comparison calls that PASS.
    """
    return {(t, n): sql for t, n, sql in conn.execute(
        "SELECT type, name, sql FROM sqlite_master "
        "WHERE type IN ('view','trigger','index') AND sql IS NOT NULL "
        "AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'")}


def deep_compare(committed_path, rebuilt_path):
    """Every table, every row — not just seven scalars.

    WHY THIS EXISTS. The core invariants are `PRAGMA user_version` plus COUNT(*)
    on six tables. An UPDATE changes no count, so the entire class of "someone
    edited values in the committed DB" is invisible to them, and so is any change
    to the 56 tables not on the list. CLAUDE.md rule 4 nonetheless says CI "fails
    on any divergence", which was never what the comparator did.
